outcome.statement: More mobile visitors who land on a public recipe page keep a recipe (save it into a Kitchen). Sprint 10 exit number: mobile LCP <= 2.5 s at Lighthouse slow-4G on /r/<slug>, /browse and /, from 7.6 / 7.7 / 6.1 s (2026-09-06 baseline). North Star: recipes kept per week, baseline captured in Sprint 10.
outcome.metric: recipes kept per week (North Star; inputs: recipe-page reach, view->save, generation+image completion, returning Kitchen use, publication); Sprint 10 gate: mobile LCP <= 2.5 s on the three public surfaces

opportunities.statement: First-time visitors cannot find the public recipes from the app's main screens: the header offers Generator / My Kitchen / Sign In, the only route is a footer link, and the empty Kitchen points only at the generator
opportunities.evidence: Observed task failure (non-author participant, phone, 'go to the public recipes'); Claude walkthrough 2026-09-06 steps 1, 2, 6 (footer link at y=875 in an 844 px viewport)

solutions.statement: Persistent top navigation with real links (Generator, My Kitchen, Browse) on SPA and SSR, mobile-collapsible, replacing the button-only header

tests.assumption: A first-time visitor finds public recipes unprompted within 30 s when Browse is in the header (2 of 3 phone walkthroughs, before/after)
Real anchors are crawlable and open-in-new-tab works
tests.type: gstack snapshot: header items are <a href>, not <button>

solutions.statement: Empty-Kitchen state and post-save state offer a 'Browse public recipes' call to action next to 'Go to Generator'

tests.assumption: Guests who land in an empty Kitchen reach /browse without scrolling
tests.type: gstack walkthrough: CTA visible above the fold at 390x844

solutions.statement: Symmetrical footer carrying the same primary links on SPA and SSR, so the bottom of any page is also a way out

tests.assumption: Footer links are identical across / , /kitchen, /browse, /r/<slug>
tests.type: snapshot diff across the four surfaces

opportunities.statement: On a phone a visitor sees at most one recipe at a time; browse is 13,122 px tall for 20 cards and the SPA home shows no recipe at all above the fold
opportunities.evidence: gstack browse at 390x844 on /browse and / (2026-09-06; reproducible with the viewport + screenshot commands in product-grill-2026-09-06.md, Evidence baseline): 0 complete cards above the fold on /browse, the one visible image still blank at 5 s, 0 recipes on /; Kitchen grid is 1 column under the sm breakpoint

solutions.statement: Compact 2-up cards with small thumbnails on /browse and the Kitchen below the sm breakpoint

tests.assumption: >= 4 recipe cards fully visible above the fold at 390x844 on /browse and in a Kitchen with 134 recipes
tests.type: gstack count of cards with bounding box inside viewport

solutions.statement: Shorter SPA shell time-to-first-paint on / (route-level code split, deferred modals, no render-blocking font import) so the first screen is content, not a 6 s blank

tests.assumption: FCP on / <= 2.0 s at slow-4G (from 6.0 s)

opportunities.statement: Recipe images take 5+ seconds to appear on a throttled connection and pages look broken while they load; every image is a 0.9-1.8 MB full-resolution PNG/JPEG with no variants, no dimensions, and the SSR hero (the LCP element) is lazy-loaded
opportunities.evidence: Lighthouse 2026-09-06: LCP 7.6 s /r/<slug>, 7.7 s /browse; curl Content-Length on 7 images; recipe.html:38 loading=lazy on hero

solutions.statement: Resized image variants (thumb/card/hero, WebP) generated at upload or on first request and served with width/height, srcset/sizes, fetchpriority=high on the hero, lazy only below the fold

tests.assumption: LCP <= 2.5 s on /r/<slug> and /browse at slow-4G; above-the-fold image bytes <= 150 KB
Variants are cache-busted correctly by the existing ?v= hash and the 24 h Cache-Control

solutions.statement: Low-quality placeholder (blurred tiny variant or dominant-colour box) painted in the fixed 4:3 container until the real image arrives

tests.assumption: CLS stays 0 and the placeholder paints before 1 s at slow-4G

solutions.statement: Interim: Express-side resizing proxy over the existing PNGs (sharp), so the LCP number lands before the full variant pipeline

tests.assumption: Proxy resize p95 < 300 ms and Cloud Run memory stays under the 1 Gi limit
tests.type: Datadog express-frontend latency + Cloud Run memory metric

children.statement: The origin itself adds up to 9 s to an image request whenever the Flask Valkey client's IAM token has expired (33-37 min tokens, fixed 45 min refresh)
children.evidence: KAN-268 / RCP-98: Datadog 51% redis.command errors, image endpoint p95 9.6-11 s; Cloud Logging timeline

solutions.statement: Expiry-aware token refresh plus refresh-and-retry-once on AuthenticationError, and no redis-py retry on a dead credential (KAN-268)

tests.assumption: redis.command error rate < 1% and PING p50 < 50 ms over 24 h in prod; image endpoint p95 < 2 s

solutions.statement: Alternative: drop the Valkey read-through on the image path and rely on Cloud CDN / Cache-Control alone

tests.assumption: Image p95 < 2 s without the cache layer
tests.type: Datadog APM aggregate after a flag flip on staging preview

opportunities.statement: With 95 public and 134 personal recipes across dozens of cookbooks, there is no way to narrow or order a list: the SPA has no search/sort, /browse takes only ?page, and the home page advertises a schema.org SearchAction that nothing implements
opportunities.evidence: Inspection: kitchen.component.ts filters by cookbook membership only; public_bp.py:492 reads ?page only; index.html:101-106 dead SearchAction

solutions.statement: Client-side filter and sort in the Kitchen (text, tag, cookbook, prep+cook time; newest / A-Z / quickest) over the already-loaded list

tests.assumption: 'Find the dessert recipes' completes in <= 30 s in a 134-recipe Kitchen on a phone

solutions.statement: Server-side query parameters on /browse (q, tag, sort) rendered by SSR with canonical/robots handling, making the SearchAction true

tests.assumption: Filtered/sorted browse pages return 200, are cached, and do not create duplicate-content indexing (canonical or noindex on filtered views)

opportunities.statement: Nothing measures whether any of this changes user behaviour: no analytics, no RUM, and a privacy policy that promises usage analytics and an opt-out that do not exist
opportunities.evidence: Datadog: 0 RUM apps; grep: no analytics in src/ server/ Backend/; privacy-policy.html:212,385

solutions.statement: Datadog RUM in the SPA and SSR pages at 100% sampling with custom actions for the five North Star inputs, behind a consent toggle wired to trackingConsent

tests.assumption: All five inputs (recipe-page reach, view->save, generation+image completion, returning Kitchen use, publication) are queryable in Datadog within one week of release, and declining consent stops all RUM traffic
tests.type: Datadog RUM query + network tab with consent declined

solutions.statement: First-party event endpoint (POST /api/events) writing to Cloud SQL, no third-party script

tests.assumption: Same five inputs queryable via SQL; endpoint rate-limited and schema-validated

opportunities.statement: A UI change cannot be seen on a real phone over a real connection until it reaches production; staging deploys are a manual workflow run of one branch
opportunities.evidence: staging-deploy.yml workflow_dispatch; last run 2026-09-04; Sprint 9 retro action 2 (Cloud Deploy, approach decided by Adam)

solutions.statement: Per-PR preview URLs on staging via Cloud Run revision tags (--tag pr-N --no-traffic) on the Cloud Deploy path (KAN-250 remaining scope, KAN-227)

tests.assumption: A pushed PR yields a staging preview URL within 10 minutes and gstack/Lighthouse can target it
tests.type: workflow run + curl of the tagged revision URL

solutions.statement: Keep the manual dispatch and add a branch input so any branch can be deployed to the single staging pair

tests.assumption: Manual dispatch with a branch input deploys and reports the URL

opportunities.statement: Power users want control over generation defaults (servings, units, image generation, model), currently fixed server-side
opportunities.evidence: Hypothesis, n=1 (Adam). Plumbing exists: server/validation.ts optional model field, generation_api_bp.py data.get('model'), GET /api/models curated list

solutions.statement: Settings tab: default servings, metric/imperial, image generation on/off, model picker bound to an explicit server-owned GA allowlist from GET /api/models; KAN-269 must add release-channel filtering before the picker because the current endpoint only filters capabilities. Preview, experimental, and moving latest aliases are excluded. Eval spec (12-prompt golden set, 12/12 schema-valid on first attempt, p95 <= 20 s, fallback to default) written into the PRD first

tests.assumption: Every offered model is on the explicit GA allowlist and passes all 12 golden-set prompts schema-valid on the first attempt
tests.type: Backend pytest for the endpoint allowlist + recorded-fixture eval in CI + manual live dispatch

tests.assumption: The settings tab is used by at least one non-author user within 4 weeks of first users
